issues.legal_issue: Delay and laches do not bar a challenge to land acquisition where substantial procedural illegality affecting the constitutional right to property is alleged.

Participation by landowners in acquisition proceedings may establish implied notice, so failure to serve individual notice alone does not invalidate an acquisition when the owners had actual knowledge and were not prejudiced.
Failure to provide the required notice and opportunity to be heard to recorded landowners invalidates an acquisition notification when that failure prejudices their rights.
Compensation agreed to by landowners may be validly determined where the competent authority accepts the agreement by issuing an order fixing the agreed amount.

For land vested or taken into possession before the commencement of the transitional provisions, compensation must be tendered and paid within the prescribed six-month period to preserve the acquisition.
Possession cannot be transferred to the acquiring trust before it deposits the compensation determined under the governing statute.
